newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Sandinistas hold property protest in Nicaragua.
newsitem.headline: Sandinistas hold property protest in Nicaragua.

text.p: Hundreds of pro-Sandinista protesters marched on Nicaragua's National Assembly on Tuesday to demand legal titles for thousands of families who possess confiscated property, and a halt to a wave of evictions.

Leaders of the 300 protesters promised to resist attempts by the right-wing government of President Arnoldo Aleman, which took power on Jan. 10, to roll back the land reforms carried out by the 1979-1990 leftist Sandinista government.

They demanded that parliament pass a law suspending a wave of court-ordered evictions of people who received confiscated land during the Sandinista government until stalled talks with the government to resolve the property problem have concluded.
"The first step is to stop the evictions; to stop this climate of violence the government is creating," Sandinista Congressman Victor Hugo Tinoco told the protesters.

They also demanded the government legalise the ownership of about 120,000 families awarded property by the Sandinistas in a flurry of disputed legislation before leaving power after their 1990 electoral defeat by former President Violeta Chamorro.

At issue in the property dispute were a total of more than 200,000 houses, farms and businesses confiscated by the Sandinistas, many of which are being reclaimed by their former owners through Nicaragua's courts.

The march followed Monday's warning by former Sandinista president Daniel Ortega of a "total war" over property if the National Assembly, which is controlled by Aleman's Liberal Alliance, does not order a halt to the evictions.

Talks between the Sandinistas and the government over the property issue were suspended on Feb. 27 and Ortega said if the government does not stop the evictions the Sandinistas would call off the talks for good.
